html:
The Badjiri, also written Budjari, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the country just north of the Paroo River, near the southern border of Queensland. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

They are not the same as the Bidjara peoples further north. Their land is semi-arid, with rivers that flow only after rain and waterholes that people knew in detail. Neighbours on the map include the Kullilla, the Kunja and the Margany. Sheep and cattle stations reached the Paroo in the 1860s and 1870s. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
